sample_unit: tumor board cases (first-diagnosis pancreatic cancer patients)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy versus tumor board decisions, including category-specific recall
links.effect: Best accuracy 78.6% (micro-F1 0.786) for advanced zero-shot and CoT, but Recall NEO = 0.00 (0/7); few-shot Recall NEO = 1.00 with overall accuracy 56.7%.
links.quote: Crucially, both high-accuracy strategies failed to identify any of the neoadjuvant therapy candidates (Recall NEO = 0.00; 0/7 cases), systematically misclassifying them as palliative or surgical.

links.outcome: Whether aggregate accuracy conceals poor category-specific performance
links.effect: Overall accuracy of 78.6% masked zero recall for neoadjuvant candidates (0/7); aggregate metrics hid a critical class-specific failure.
links.quote: The high global accuracy masks a significant safety limitation regarding the recognition of complex, intermediate-stage patients.

unlisted_practices: Comparing prompting strategies (zero-shot, chain-of-thought, few-shot) for LLM oncology treatment decision prediction

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates an LLM on real tumor board cases across different prompting strategies (guardrails/deployment techniques) to assess decision-making accuracy and safety pitfalls.
